Mark matrix verified by pdftotext -bbox column binning against header centres plus vector rule-line geometry; agrees with the visual read except the merged Adverse Event / Concomitant Treatments cell, resolved from the rule lines. table_metadata.table_purpose: Main schedule of assessments: screening, baseline, 12-week treatment period, follow-up and early termination
table_metadata.notes: Single table; doc p.91 carries only the numbered footnotes (no activity rows). One label column (L=1), data columns at positions 2-9. Rows 34 (Adverse Event or Intercurrent Illness) and 35 (Previous and Concomitant Treatments) share one data cell ruled across columns 2-9 and both rows, holding a single 'x': distributed to both rows and all eight columns (source_range 2:9). The two label cells are separated by their own rule line.

schedule_properties.property_comment: Unlabelled top band; its only value 'Treatment Period' is a merged cell spanning the Week 2 to Week 12 columns (positions 4-7); the cells over Screening, Baseline, Follow-Up Visit and Early Termination Visit are blank. Typed epoch because the spanning value names a major study phase (§3); name synthesised as the fixed name of the type because the label cell is empty.

Named visits (Screening, Baseline, Week 2, Week 6, Week 9, Week 12, Follow-Up Visit, Early Termination Visit); printed row label 'Visit' carries footnote 8 (visit schedule relative to Day 1), which applies to the whole row.

Study days per visit relative to first study drug administration (Day 1): ranges for Screening (-28 to -8) and Baseline (-7 to -1), single target days with a printed window for later visits (e.g. '14 (± 7)'), and '(NA)' for Early Termination. The window qualifier is printed inside each cell and stays in the cell value (§3); typed study_day from the printed label and values.

annotations.annotation_text: First study drug administration should be one day after the last baseline assessment.
Physical examination includes weight, heart and respiratory rate, and body temperature.

All women will have serum pregnancy tests performed at screening and baseline. A urine pregnancy test will also be done at baseline prior to randomization. All women of childbearing potential will have serum and urine pregnancy tests at each subsequent visit.
The same salivary or tear sample is used for volume and biomarker assessments (see Section 4.6.1.3.4.).
Only markers required for ESSDAI scoring will be collected.
Safety laboratory assessment consists of hematology, blood chemistry, coagulation, lipids and urinalysis.
MSG biopsies procedures for the optional substudy may be performed at separate study center visits providing the procedures are carried out within the windows specified for the main study.

Screening, baseline and on-treatment visit schedules are all relative to the first day of study drug administration (Day 1). The follow-up visit is scheduled relative to the Week 12 end-of-treatment visit (+14 days after the end-of-treatment visit [± 7 days]).
